directAnswer: An email address may not work due to incorrect spelling, server issues, or account suspension. Verify the address and check your email provider's status.
summary: There are several reasons why an email address might not function properly, including user error, server problems, or account restrictions.

sections.heading: Common Issues
sections.body: Common problems include misspellings in the email address, incorrect domain names, or the recipient's inbox being full.

sections.heading: Server Status
sections.body: Check your email provider's status page for outages or maintenance that might affect email delivery.

sections.heading: Account Status
sections.body: Ensure that the email account is active and not suspended due to policy violations or inactivity.

steps.title: Verify Email Address
steps.detail: Double-check the spelling of the email address and ensure it follows the correct format (e.g., user@example.com).

steps.title: Check Email Provider Status
steps.detail: Visit the status page of your email provider (e.g., Gmail, Outlook) to see if there are any ongoing issues.

steps.title: Test Sending to Another Address
steps.detail: Try sending an email to a different address to determine if the issue is with the specific email address or your account.

faqs.question: What should I do if my email is bouncing back?
faqs.answer: Check the bounce-back message for clues about the issue, such as an invalid address or full inbox.

faqs.question: How can I recover a suspended email account?
faqs.answer: Contact your email provider's support team for assistance with account recovery and reinstatement.

faqs.question: Why does my email provider say the address doesn't exist?
faqs.answer: This usually means the email address is misspelled, the domain is incorrect, or the account has been deleted.

caveats: Email delivery issues can vary by provider and may require specific troubleshooting steps based on the service.
